recalls.title: CHE-US Recalls Magnetic Robot Toys Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Magnet Ingestion; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys
recalls.hazard_summary: The recalled magnetic stick figures violate the mandatory standard for toys because when pulled apart, the figures’ arms and legs liberate high-powered magnets posing an ingestion hazard to children. When high-powered magnets are swallowed, the ingested magnets can attract each other, or other metal objects, and become lodged in the digestive system. This can result in perforations, twisting, and/or blockage of the intestines, blood poisoning and death.
recalls.retailers:
Sold Online At:
Amazon.com from April 2025 through August 2026 for between t $9 and $18.
recalls.remedy: Consumers should stop using the stick figures immediately, take them away from children and contact CHE-US for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to send a photo of the toys in the trash to CHE-USMagneticRobotToysRecall@outlook.com. Consumers should then dispose of the recalled product.

recalls.title: Cipton Recalls Bicycle Helmets Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Head Injury; Violate Mandatory Standard for Bicycle Helmets
recalls.hazard_summary: The recalled helmets violate the mandatory safety standard for bicycle helmets because the helmets do not comply with the impact attenuation, positional stability and certification requirements. The helmets can fail to protect the user in the event of a crash, posing a serious risk of injury or death due to head injury.
recalls.retailers: Dicks Sporting Goods and JC Penny nationwide and online at Dickssportinggoods.com from April 2024 through May 2026 for about $35.
recalls.remedy:
Consumers should stop using the helmets immediately and contact Cipton for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to destroy the helmet by cutting the straps and writing in permanent marker “Recalled” on the helmet and send a photo of the destroyed helmet to Reply@customersupport123.com. Consumers should then dispose of the recalled product. 


Note: Do not throw this defective lithium-ion battery or device in the trash, the general recycling stream (e.g., street-level or curbside recycling bins), or in used battery recycling boxes found at various retail and home improvement stores. Defective lithium-ion batteries must be disposed of differently than other batteries, because they present a greater risk of fire. Your municipal household hazardous waste (HHW) collection center may accept this defective lithium-ion battery or device for disposal. If it does not, contact your municipality for further guidance.
